Perhaps I'm confused but I think it would be a good idea to let him know exactly what's going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the first witness, the evidence that I read out, I decline to say who that was and I submit it shouldn't be done. With respect to the next one, I'm prepared to do so and that would be a question of moving into the private session in the way that Your Honour mentioned at an earlier stage, although I must say I have some legal concerns about it. That's really a matter for the bench to decide. But in respect of this witness perhaps I could ask that we move into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now I'm going to put some evidence from the first witness that I meant -- I didn't mention their name but the first witness that I put something to you from. And this, now, Your Honours, is at 18th of February 2005, at page 24 of the transcript. Sorry, just excuse me one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, just excuse me, sorry, we are just going to reorganise that. I'm sorry, Your Honours, I'll come to that passage. I found that we are halfway through it. It's unfair to the witness to put that halfway bit so we'll find the start of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right, I'm going to put another witness to you now. This is a witness from the 16th of February 2005, at page 31. And this witness was questioned in the following way at page -- at line 17: Question: "Very well. Upon arrival at Jablanica, your commander, Ramiz Delalic, was still present with the unit for at least some type of your stop at Jablanica; is that correct?" Answer: "In Donja Jablanica. He stayed in Donja Jablanica, in Zuka's base, as far as I know." Question: "Yes. Well, you're correct to correct me." It was in fact -- "well, it's the fact that your unit arrived with Ramiz Delalic at Donja Jablanica and stopped there for a period of time. Is that correct?" Answer: "15, 20 minutes approximately." Now, the evidence I've just put to you there, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, just excuse me a moment, please, and I'll return with another piece of transcript. Okay. All right. Now, I'm going to put another piece of evidence and this one I think the name can be given without any difficulty. Your Honours, this was on the 15th of February 2005, at page 5. This is evidence given by Erdin Arnautovic in this Court. I should ask you this question about Erdin Arnautovic. When you were in prison on the last occasion, Erdin Arnautovic used to come and visit you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And he's a friend of yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, he says something different: Question: All right, in fact in fairness to you I'm going to put this: Question: "I now take you to Jablanica itself." Your Honour that starts on page 4. "I now take you to Jablanica itself. And I put to you that when you arrived in Jablanica, Ramiz Delalic also arrived there; is that correct?" Answer: "No. He remained in Konjic." Question: "All right. Is it your evidence that he did not go to Jablanica on that morning of the 8th of September? Is that your position?" Answer: "He went as far as Konjic and then he remained in Konjic with Malco Rovcanin and Fikret Kajevic and then he arrived later on." Question: "Yes. Well, in the statement that you made on the 3rd of December 1998 to the cantonal court in Sarajevo," and this is at page 2, Your Honours, that's a quote from the text, I interpose, "did you say this," and this is about ten lines from the top. Quote. Mr. Delalic the passage I'm about to read out now is a quote from a statement of Mr. Arnautovic on a previous occasion. Quote: "I was going into the village of Grabovica but Rovcanin, Malco, Delalic, Ramiz, and Kajevic, Fikret, remained at Jablanica because of additional agreeing with officers of other units that were to take part in the action." End of quote. Question by me: "Now, did you say that to the cantonal court back in 1998?" Answer: "I do not recognise the cantonal court because the police and judiciary are all corrupt, they are all saying and writing false things. I do not accept any statements made before those courts." Now, my question to you is this: Were you aware that or do you know, that Erdin Arnautovic had made a statement to the cantonal court in 1998 when he said you went to Jablanica but stayed there with Malco and Fikret Kajevic for additional agreeing with other commanders? Did you know that he made such a statement?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you know why it is that having made that statement in 1998, he then changed it in this Court to say or changed his position in this Court to say that you stopped in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not something this witness can --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's okay. Your Honour, it may be correct what my friend says, technically. I want to give the witness to opportunity to comment but if my friend objects, frankly, I -- she's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Sorry, just excuse me once more. Very well. At page 93 on the 17th of February, a witness was being cross-examined and the question was this at line 20: Question: "I'd like to ask you now a few questions about your accommodation as you arrived in the village of Grabovica. You've indicated that Ramiz Delalic, Celo, told the soldiers to go and accommodate themselves in two empty houses; is that right?" Sorry, that's a wrong quote. "Is that so?" Answer: "Yes." Question: "Are you able to point at those two houses in a picture?" And then the witness indicated certain houses which I won't trouble you with now. Now, that evidence that you've just heard read out, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was the question directed to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, it was, Mr. Delalic. The evidence you've just heard me read --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't sure any more because you are putting questions left and right so I wasn't sure whether it applied to me. Could you put it again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. Of course I can. The passage I'm reading now commences at line 20. Question. I'll just explain so that there is no doubt about it. I'm going to read you questions and answers and then I'll ask you a question. Question: "I'd like to ask you now a few questions about your accommodation as you arrived in the village of Grabovica. You've indicated that Ramiz Delalic, Celo, told the soldiers to go and accommodate themselves in two empty houses, is that so?" Answer: "Yes." Question: "Are you able to point to those two houses if shown a picture?" Answer: "I should hope so. I just hope it's going to be a larger photograph because on one side of the road there was a small hill." Then other questions were asked. Now, Mr. Delalic, however I've stopped quoting now and now I'm asking you a direct question. That evidence I've just read out to you, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was a senior officer of the BH army and it wasn't possible for me to travel with the troops on a bus. I travelled in a car. So it's not true that I travelled with the troops on a bus. As for the other allegations, it isn't true. I had even no idea where Grabovica was and where the soldiers would be billeted. So that's not true what you said about me showing some houses and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But Mr. Delalic, even apart from all of this, you have admitted this in the past you were shown Grabovica through binoculars by Zulfikar Alispahic on an earlier occasion, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfikar didn't show it to me. Nihad Bojadzic did but on that occasion, he didn't tell me the name. He just said that there was a village and that the line had been moved, but he didn't tell me what the village was called. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go on now. I'm going to put some more from there witness. This is at the 18th of February, page 24. At line 7, question -- sorry, line 2. "Good morning. I'd like to take you back" -- and this is the question. "I'd like to take you back to where I left you last night. You were telling the Trial Chamber about your arrival in Grabovica and Ramiz Delalic, Celo, asking the troops to go and accommodate themselves into empty houses. Do you remember that?" Answer: "Yes." Question: "Having given that order, Celo then promptly left Grabovica, isn't that the case, sir?" Answer: "Yes." Question: "And only after Celo had left did someone from the 9th Brigade look for alternative accommodation, isn't that so?" Answer: "Yes." Now, I've finished reading that evidence out, Mr. Delalic, and that part of the evidence that I just read out to you, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because the real truth about this is you did go to Jablanica, you did go to Grabovica, and only after you'd been to Grabovica with your troops, in the morning of the 9th -- sorry, the morning of the -- let me start that question again. You did go to Jablanica in the morning of the 8th of September and you did go to Grabovica shortly after that, and only after they started to take up position in houses did you leave Grabovica and go somewhere else. Is that true or is it false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all I'd like to say that all of these attempts of yours to attribute something to me is something that you have already tried to do that through you, through your assistants and through the gentleman sitting next to you, you even tried some bribery for me to say that I didn't see Sefer here, that I didn't do this. I even have the tapes recorded during interviews with your lawyers. You offered money and so on. And this will be subject of an investigation perhaps by this very Prosecution. Here you're trying to expand on some things and to turn them into extreme allegations. My reply to that is no. This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where are those tapes?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met the investigator in Sarajevo and I told them that I had a tape and I could take it with me. I asked should I? I was told no, no need for that. If there will be any need we will let you know. So I didn't take the tape with me. I have a tape recorded during the interview with one of your lawyers and some other lawyers who tried to convince me in various ways to change my statement. This was done by several lawyers who offered me money and so on. The Court, if they wish me to bring the tape, I will bring it. One tape was made during the interview with attorney Azem Mehonjic, who is an attorney in Sarajevo. I have that interview recorded. We sat in a cafe where music played and it was a bit loud. However, I believe that this institution has technical means necessary in order to play this properly, and if there is any need, I will send the tape in. As for your assistant sitting next to you, he came to see me while I was at the central prison, towards the end of my sentence there. He also suggested to me not to mention Sefer. He said that the Court and the Prosecutor operate in such a way that they would first indict Sefer and then after that they will indict others including myself and that therefore I should not say any of the things that could compromise Sefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic is your position this? You will smear anyone who has the possibility to hurt you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You'll smear Halilovic, Karavelic, Hodzic, the lawyers, anyone who hurts you, correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Whereas in reality, you yourself, despite fighting bravely in the war, are in effect nowadays an underworld figure and a habitual criminal. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't have opinions. I'm putting questions to you. Have you recently claimed in the press in Sarajevo that there is a contract out upon you put there by the Albanian Mafia?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And while on release on bail for the murder charge that you're facing, did you become involved in a fight with an Albanian, a senior Albanian criminal and find yourself locked up overnight in the police cells?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, since you were released from prison on bail for the murder charge, weren't you in a fight with a man called Keljmendi, Naser?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I would like to clarify this question before the Trial Chamber, I think we need to go into private session because this is the subject of an investigation currently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well that's an appropriate thing to ask for. I ask that we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, there is one matter that I want to ask you. You mentioned that there were -- you were a witness in a case -- well, I'll restructure now the question. Never mind what you mentioned. Let me ask you the question just in the abstract. Were you in a witness in a case involving murder, supposedly committed by the director of the AID?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not wish to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Can we move into the private session, if that's the case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Delalic. Now, concerning -- just excuse me a moment. I want to put some propositions to you here about what happened at -- excuse me one second. Moving to another topic now, Your Honours. I don't know if this is a good time to take a break or not, but the next topic will be a sizeable one. For my own purposes I prefer not to break it up so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could take a break now and we will resume at 25 minutes to 1, 30-minutes break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Sorry, I can't hear. Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Delalic. Could I just ask now that the witness be shown D222? That's the official note filed by a man named Salihamidzic, Ahmed, which was tendered into evidence here some time ago. Mr. Delalic we are now going back to Grabovica and what's going to be on the screen in front of you now is a document headed "official note." Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. This is an official note that we are told was compiled on or about the 12th of September 1993 and it's in evidence and I'm going to put some allegations from it to you. Now, would you please look to the second paragraph -- sorry, look to a sentence that begins, with the sentence "at around 1500 hours on the same day I went with the military police Commander Sead Kurt to Grabovica." Could you just tell me when you find that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Delalic, it's the fact, isn't it, that the police -- that Salihamidzic and the man named Kurt came to Grabovica at around 1500 hours or a little bit after that in a marked police car on the 9th of September, true or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I put it to you further that you saw them arrive in a marked police car near to Adnan Solakovic's base in the village. True or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Didn't see that police car?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed. "We interviewed" -- look at the start of the next -- sorry, no, we'll go on from there. I apologise. I'm going to take you through it solidly here. Okay. You see it says here, "we arrived" -- "when we arrived at the building of the former Grabovica railway station, we were stopped by an armed soldier at an improvised checkpoint." Now, I want to ask you this: There was, in fact, an improvised checkpoint right outside Adnan Solakovic's house, his base, in the afternoon of the 9th of September, true or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a guard post there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And it was manned by a Croatian soldier, wasn't it? An army of Bosnia and Herzegovina soldier but one of Croatian background, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: A very terrified and scared soldier, I put to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well, let's go on with this report. The report says "we had to show our identity cards. We were allowed through. To a flat where Ivan Pranjic and his wife Stoja lived." Now, did you ever meet Ivan Pranjic and his wife Stoja?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just move down, he then says "we met two other persons, two unknown civilians. In speaking to them we established that one of them was the commander of an independent battalion." Then there's a bit of handwriting saying Solakovic but you can disregard that, although I'll ask you a question about it. "And the other was a displaced person from Stolac named Zulfo." Now, the first question is: Did you meet Zulfo yourself?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That name is not familiar to me. Perhaps I did meet him but I really don't know this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In the middle of the afternoon of the -- of September the 9th, Adnan Solakovic was in that village, wasn't he, at his command house?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go further. "We interviewed these persons and we learned that at the aforesaid time, soldiers from the unit commanded by Ramiz Delalic, also known as Celo, who were billeted 100 metres downstream killed the following persons in Malidja Kirce [phoen]," which I think is translated the "Maric houses." And then some names are given. First of all, is it the fact that those troops were from a unit commanded by you or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's move further. You see a sentence the bodies of the women, Luca, Mare, and Ruzica, had reportedly been seen in a fallow field by Marinko Maric's house while Marinko Maric's body was reportedly in a ravine between the house where we conducted the interview and Crno Vrelo, about 300 metres upstream. Now, did you see those bodies of those women in the fallow field?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Text goes on: During the interview, intermittent shots could be heard coming from the direction of Marica Kurce [phoen]. When you were in the village, did you hear intermittent shots being fired?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Keep going: We were advised by -- perhaps I should ask a question here. Somebody may have interposed the word Solakovic or "Sokalovic" in there, as you see. There was no Sokolovic who was the commander of the 2nd Independent Battalion but the commander was Adnan Solakovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. But you do know, don't you, that the 2nd Independent Battalion was commanded by a man called Adnan Solakovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's proceed. "We were" -- I'm reading now from the passage, "We were advised by Commander Sokolovic," it says, "that it was not possible to protect the lives of Ivan Pranjic and his wife Stoja without the use of weapons. And it was recommended that we should try to organise an evacuation of Croatian inhabitants from this part of Grabovica. Because of this and for personal security reasons we did not go to that part of the suburb where Celo's units were billeted which was about 100 metres downstream." Did you yourself know that there were two old Croatian civilians hiding in the house of Adnan Solakovic in the middle of the afternoon on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you in the village at the time when the police came to visit the Adnan Solakovic house and saw these two old people there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I saw them, and I stayed there very briefly, I didn't see the police car or anything like that. I doubt that they even came. I didn't really see anything when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, pardon me. Just excuse me. Sorry about that. Very well. Well, let's proceed then. "When we left we spoke with the soldier who was at the guard post and who had checked our identity cards earlier, and he told us that the troops next to them were killing people and he feared for his own life because he was not a Muslim." I want to ask you again: Did you meet that guard, did you meet a guard, outside Adnan Solakovic's base in the middle of the afternoon of the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Adnan Solakovic had members of the Croat ethnic group, but I don't think that I actually met him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see a terrified individual guarding the Solakovic house when you were present?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I spent any time in front of Adnan Solakovic's house, and if I did, I don't recall seeing a terrified guard or anybody like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's press on. This police officer goes on to say, "On our return we stopped at Crno Vrelo and in an attempt to find the body of Marinko Maric we searched a wide area below the road. I went down to the Neretva River and searched the terrain there but found nothing. While I was in the Neretva canyon, Sead Kurt stayed by the car in the road and Celo came along in a car and asked him whether we found anything. He then added 'You're looking for them yet look at what they are doing with our people.'" Now that lass passage I've just read out to you about you coming along in a car and saying those things, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because what happened was that you saw the police down at Adnan Solakovic and you drove up to see what they were doing, correct or wrong?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see a police car that day at all, not even in passing, and not at all at the house where Adnan Solakovic was staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what about on the iron bridge as you go out of Grabovica back towards Jablanica? Did you see a car there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you speak to a member of the local military police and say the things that I've read out to you from this report?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where you got that from, but it's definitely not sure that I saw any police car or police officers. I arrived with Zulfikar Alispago that day and I saw what I saw. I said that and it's quite certain that I did not see a police car or any police officers and I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And furthermore, is it your evidence that the first time you went to the village, you went in a jeep with Zuka, Zulfikar Alispago? And I mean on the day, the 9th of September.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I came with him in his jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And it's your evidence that you arrived with him and you left with him, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And according to you, you came back later by yourself after you heard news about the finding of the two boys; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And according to you, you didn't see Zuka in the village after that one visit that he paid with you in the mid-afternoon on that day. Mr. Delalic, that question was a mess. I apologise for it. I'll put it another way. After you went with Zuka to the village in the middle of the afternoon, as far as you know, Zuka didn't go back to the village that day. True or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, he didn't go back to the village, according to you, when you were there, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. Okay. And after you had come back from the village with the two boys, you say he was part of this discussion where removing or hiding the dirty laundry was discussed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And after that discussion was finished, you yourself went back to stay in Grabovica; is that correct? I mean later on in the night of the 9th.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where do you say you stayed that night, the night of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I spent that night at the apartment of Zulfikar Alispago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now I've got more of this report to put to you. Could you look down -- Mr. Delalic you're going to have to indicate when you need the page to be turned over, okay? But on the English, it's on the third page, and I think it will be on the second page of the Bosnian version. So if the witness could be shown the second page of the Bosnian version, please? Do you have in front of you now a page that includes the words -- just find the passage that begins this way: At 1830 hours on the 10th of September 1993, Zulfikar Alispago of the Zulfikar unit and Edid Sarovic [phoen], the commander of the Igman Wolves unit, came to the public security station. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, they are now talking here or this man, Mr. Salihamidzic is talking that he was visited by Zuka and by Adib Saric and gave certain news and now I'm going to put that news to you. They came to the public security station and informed the SJB chief and me that during the terrain inspection, six bodies had been found on the right bank and two bodies on the left bank. Now, that's true, isn't it, Mr. Delalic? Six bodies were found on the right bank and two on the left bank, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible but I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Didn't you see these six bodies on the right bank?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see the two bodies on the left bank?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right bank, on the approach to Grabovica, before the village, as soon as you cross the railroad bridge, about 50 or a hundred metres after that, Zuka noticed, as I said, some traces as if somebody had been pulling a bloody corpse, and this was in the middle of the street. And we followed this trail and together we found a part of a body out of the water and another part of the body in the water. So it was the body was partially immersed in water and it's possible that there were also two bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was the second body on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that place, it seemed as if there was one body or two bodies there and I said that right at the beginning. I wasn't sure if there was one body there or two bodies. We didn't go down to the water's edge. We were on the road and this was some seven or eight metres lower down. There were some bushes there so it wasn't possible to see for sure whether it was one body or two bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it possible to see whether they had any -- whether body or bodies had wounds on them, injuries?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you certainly wouldn't have been in a position to say that these bodies had entry and exit gun wounds, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't see any wounds. I saw blood. There was a lot of blood on the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, just to clarify that, as I have to, did you see blood on the bodies as well or not? The body or bodies?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't say. The body was partially immersed in water and a part of it was out of the water. And like I said there was a lot of blood on the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. I understand that. Apart from that body or bodies, you didn't see any other bodies in Grabovica at all. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And all right. Let's keep going with what's said here. Among the bodies found on the right bank was the body of a three year old child. Did you see the body of a three year old child?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Look at the next part. 14 adults and the children were evacuated alive from the right bank and taken away. Now, it's your position, isn't it, that indeed two children were evacuated alive from the right bank and taken away, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it was courtesy of you that those two were taken away, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you've also made a claim, haven't you, that at a discussion between Halilovic, Zuka and a variety of other wrongdoers, the plan was made to hide the dirty laundry. In fact, you say that plan was made and discussed on the late afternoon of the 9th of September, at Zuka's base, when you brought the children, correct or wrong?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But what you have here on this page is Zulfikar Alispago and Edib Saric of the Igman Wolves coming and telling the police about those two children, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, you made up and invented this story about Zuka and Halilovic saying -- to hide the dirty laundry, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make up anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, you know, as a matter of absolute truth, don't you, that Zuka's unit or a representative of Zuka's unit, in fact took a statement from those two boys, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Nihad Bojadzic took a statement from the two boys.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And indeed, you yourself at a subsequent time went and got a copy of that statement from Nihad Bojadzic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do it until much, much later. I got it five to six years later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That was at a time when you were helping Mr. Nikolai Mikhailov in the investigation, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you provided it to Nikolai Mikhailov, didn't you, this statement?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had that statement in my possession, and as I believed that that statement ought to reach The Hague investigators, I turned it over together with all other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's the fact. Could I just ask you to have a look at a photocopy of a document and see if you can identify it as that. And while I do I'm just going to explain some things to the Judges but if you -- you can listen to that, but also just inspect this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, lest it seem that this is another attempt to claim that the Prosecutors haven't given a statement, the fact is they have. This is on the material disclosed to us long ago. It's on the CD. It's a joint statement of Goran and Zoran Zadro. Sorry, Your Honours, I think the Prosecutors are indicating they don't have it. I didn't bring copies because it was -- it's a document that was actually disclosed by them to us. I'm happy to provide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we put it in the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honours, what I had in mind was just to -- could I just indicate -- could I deal with that in one second before we go to the ELMO? Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know if you can remember at this length of time, Mr. Delalic, but is that the document you were given?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read this but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps the best approach would be this. Could I leave that with you? It's probably a bit unfair to do it in Court now. Could I just leave that printoff with you and you have a look later on when we finish today and I'll ask you some more questions about it tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I just indicate this is a document I hadn't uploaded because it's a statement provided by the Prosecutors. But we will do that overnight. We'll have it uploaded because it's a statement we have not been dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If not I believe that you have to prepare the hard copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- to the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will do that and could I just indicate I had the intention of tendering this document even though it's a statement, not as to the truth or otherwise of its contents but just because it's -- if this witness -- if the witness when he's had a fair chance to look at it decides to say that "Yes, that the document I got," then I would tender it just as a part of what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll make that decision or deal with this issue when we have a chance to read that document. Maybe tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could I just give the Prosecutors the ERN number so that it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's -- it's ETRR 271787-RR 271788. That's the English, and it would be -- there would be markings on what's been given to the witness but anyway it will be -- once they have that they should be able to find. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we have a solution for this particular document, but I would still like to put it on record that even when a document is being used by the Defence, which we have disclosed, I think the Defence should provide us with a hard copy in Court because our case manager is a magician but she cannot just conjure up from the thousands of documents that we have disclosed to the -- I mean, there are so many documents in the EDS suite we cannot simply come up and produce the document immediately for our reference and I think counsel has been made aware of this situation. Your Honour did rule that they don't have to give us the documents in advance. I think it's sheer courtesy that they provide us with a hard copy and not say, Well, you gave it to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Morrissey has already promised us that we will have it uploaded or otherwise furnish the hard copy to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours could I just indicate this -- it wasn't on the EDS, the monster, it's on the material that was disclosed to us as witness statements, which is a confined thing. However, I've got an English copy. I'll give that to the Prosecutor right now so there need be no difficulty. That's the only one I have frankly at the moment but -- anyway it will come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Delalic, that's procedural warfare that goes on and I apologise for delaying the questions with you. But having looked at that document there, does it -- are you able to say from your memory now whether that is the document or would you just like some more time to think about it later on and tell us tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be fine, yes. You can give me the document and that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Good. Okay. Anyway, to come back to the fact it is the fact, isn't it, that Bojadzic or at least some person from the -- from the Zulfikar unit took a statement from those boys, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took the statement from the boys.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note could the witness repeat the previous answer? It is possible that he meant something else and that we misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The interpreters just asked to you repeat again what you just said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: About the documents being given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nihad Bojadzic took the statement, at least that's what I heard, and I received the paper from Nihad Bojadzic at which time he told me that he had taken the statement from the boys.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. The interpreter was concerned about your answer to a previous question which was whether you were prepared to take that document and have a look at it. I had heard it, but the interpreter didn't. So would mind just saying -- are you prepared to take document and look at it or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am looking document right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. You're prepared to take it away and have a look at it later on and see if you can remember whether that's the one Bojadzic gave you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is no need because I can't read it anyway. I can't read anything here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I offer that document for tender now in any event. There is another way of demonstrating it which we'll come to later on and since it's arisen now I offer it. I don't require the Prosecutor to respond now because we'll do it at the end after I've explained to her what else we have. I can do that out of court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course because we are in the very difficult position to judge the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. And I should explain more to the Prosecutor so we will do that after court today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right I my apologise again. Let's proceed with this document here. Do you see that I -- I'm -- I've now returned to the report that's on -- thank you. Mr. Delalic, I'm now returning to the police report that's on the screen. But you can keep a copy of that Zulfikar document with you if you wish. Okay. Now this goes on to say, "we were informed that the body of a soldier whose throat was cut was found in the reservoir of the Salakovac" -- "Solakovac," sorry, "hydroelectric power station close to Sjencina. He was a soldier from the Zulfikar unit named Ivica and he was a Croat. He had come across some soldiers from Celo's unit who stopped him and demanded to see his identity card. After establishing that he was a Croat, they cut his throat and threw him into the Neretva River." Now, Mr. Delalic, that allegation about that soldier being killed by members of the 9th Brigade, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to go into private session, if possible, before I answer this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In the circumstances, Your Honour, I don't oppose it, if it has to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Delalic, where did this supposed order take place? And at what time?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we are pursuing this subject I would like to remind Mr. Morrissey that -- to advise the witness we are in open session now. If he'd like to go back to closed to complete this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will have that paragraph redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because he just repeated his words. And later on, we'll see there is any necessity to lift the confidentiality of that piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I make it quite clear that I'll make a submission about that because it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I quite understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well perhaps we go back into the private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's press on with this. Anyway at all events, one thing you'd have to consider is this, that whatever account Zulfikar Alispago is giving, he's not hiding that fact in the least, is he, that killing? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll put it another way. Look at another part of the text. "The above indicates that the killings were perpetrated by members of the unit commanded by Ramiz Delalic, also known as Celo." Do you see that passage there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, the fact is that at this point, and I'm talking now about the point referred to in the report, that is to say the 10th of -- of September, you knew that your men were potentially in big trouble, true or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you also knew that as to the killings at Grabovica, those killings were widely known in Jablanica because of the escape of and evacuation of numerous Croatian civilians to Jablanica. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is true or not, but the crime probably became known.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's not my question. You knew that the crime had become known, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose I did know, especially since there were people who managed to flee the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And not just the Croats who got away, but also Bosniak refugees who moved up and down the road from Grabovica to Jablanica, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village where the Croats were, there were no refugees. The refugees were on the other side, in the makeshift housing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But even so, well, all right. I understand what you say. But so that's the fact, isn't it, that you knew that the news was out about the killings but you knew also that the individual perpetrators had yet to be identified, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you put a question to me so that I can understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm putting to you the proposition, you knew on the 10th of September that the perpetrators, individual killers, had yet to be identified; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about the fact that the order was supposed to be issued to identify, find and arrest the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's keep going with this document. It says here that "At 2030 hours on the 10th of September 1993, I was informed by Sead Brankovic, a Mostar SDB employee that strange things were again happening in the Grabovica area. Together with the IKM security officer Namik, we called the Zulfikar unit commander and he asked us to visit him. Adib Saric was also in Zulfikar Alispago's flat. We were informed that members of the unit commanded by Celo were again causing trouble in Grabovica. A girl named Jasna who was a displaced person and who was responsible for cleaning the hutted encampment at Grabovica was raped and two other girls fled and hid with the soldiers guarding the Grabovica hydroelectric dam." Now, is that true, Mr. Delalic that units under your -- that members of the unit commanded by Celo were again causing trouble in Grabovica? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's go further. "During the interview, Ramiz Delalic also known as Celo came to the flat with his deputy and launched a scathing attack on all Jablanica inhabitants who were allegedly kicking up a fuss over a few dead Croats." Now, that's true, isn't it, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's go further. "He said he was going back to Sarajevo with his men and asked Zulfikar to provide him with cars. If he did not get them, he and his men would set off for Sarajevo on foot." Now, Mr. Delalic, it's true that you said that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "In response to" -- I'm going further now. "In response to Zulfikar's attempts to calm him down and draw his attention to the importance of the operation, Celo said Bakir and the MUP can do that with the Laste. They just strut around and don't do anything and they are useless soldiers." Now, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You better let me finish the question because it could have two meanings. I don't remember whether the Laste were really bad soldiers. What I mean is it's true that Zulfikar attempted to calm you down and that you said Bakir and -- you said those words about Bakir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that he then said "when Vehbija Karic was asked what they should do if Croats were to cause a fuss while they were billeted in their houses, he had replied, 'Kill them and chuck them into the lake.'" Did you say that to those men assembled in Zuka's flat?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Some of his men had taken this literally and this had happened as a result. Did you say that to the assembled men in the flat?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, I believe that you have to establish whether there is a meeting in the Zuka's flat first or not to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, can I just indicate that after one more question I'm going to ask that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm just putting the facts to him as facts first and then afterwards we'll see what his position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Finally, he and his -- finally, the last thing that's here, "He and his deputy then stormed out of the flat." Now, is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you in fact go to Zuka's flat on that evening of the 10th of September at a time when Zuka, Saric, Salihamidzic, Jankovic, and another man called Brankovic were present?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that evening I went to Zuka's. None of the other persons were present, and Zuka was very drunk, and he had an outburst. We stayed very briefly in the apartment, then he went, spoke with somebody on the phone. I'm sure that there is a record of that in the MUP. He went to the emergency service where he beat somebody up really badly. But as for the meeting that you're mentioning, let me tell you there was no meeting and I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment, please. Attached to this document there is another one and I would ask that we go to the next document. The next document, it's page 3, I think, page 3 in Bosnian, it will be page 4 in the English version. There is another report attached to that report which has been -- which is in evidence in this trial, Mr. Delalic, and now I have to take you to that and that will take us through to the end of today's proceedings. Do you have in front of you a document dated the 13th of September 1993 and beginning with the words, "Croats used to live in the village of Grabovica"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. A number of lines down, probably 15 or 20 you might find a sentence beginning this way, "The local Jablanica authorities and the commander of the special purposes unit Zulfikar Alispago" -- I'll just ask you to find that part and we will go on from there. Do you have that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, you see it says here: "The local Jablanica authorities and the commander of the special purposes unit, Zulfikar Alispago, also known as Zuka, agreed to evacuate the Croatian population. 18 persons were evacuated." Now that's true, isn't it, Mr. Delalic, that Zuka assisted the police and evacuated 18 persons?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just look a couple of lines down. No, I should read you the whole sentence I'm sorry. "When the deputy chief of the Jablanica police station and leader of the Jablanica military police company arrived at the spot where Marinko Maric's body was supposed to be, Ramiz Delalic, also known as Celo, approached them and asked, have you found anything? While you are busy searching for them, look what they are doing to us. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's proceed further. And I think you may need to turn over the page now. It's page 5 of the English version and it's, I think, page 4 of yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the full sentence should be read out where it says, "probably referring to the detainees from the Dretelj camp," for the sake of completeness Your Honours since everything is now being reflected on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't have any difficulty if -- it's relevance, so I will read that out further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That could be read out but this is the guess from the other person and the witness denied he made these kind of remarks. So I wonder whether it's meaningless or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I won't do it, Your Honour. I won't do it. If the Prosecutor wants to put it in re-examination, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the other page now you see there this section. "On 10th of September 1993, at about 20.30 p.m. ..." -- Do you have that section?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go on. "... I was in Zulfikar Alispago's flat in the company of the Jablanica director -- deputy police chief and an official of the military security service of the Supreme Command, Namik Dzankovic. While we were in the flat, Ramiz Delalic also known as Celo, came in. He was obviously excited. He was accompanied by his deputy whose name was Malco. He said that he had just executed one of his soldiers and threatened to withdraw his units back to Sarajevo and said that he did not care about Mostar." Now, is that true? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did Malco say that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea if I was there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did Malco say that in your presence?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Go on with it. "He cursed Minister Bakir Alispahic and his Laste unit and said that the MUP members were masquerading like dummies, that they were no good as fighters and that they should be sent to Mostar." Did you say that on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I wasn't there, I couldn't have said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think that's a very logical thing to say. But it is something that you said on other occasions, isn't it, that the Laste were a bunch of dancers or dummies, is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I said that in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I won't ask you to say it now. But it was a point of argument, wasn't it, between the army and the police sometimes that those of you who had to do the fighting felt some resentment against the police who didn't get their hands dirty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the soldiers felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. It goes on here: "He said that he'd asked Vehbija Karic what he should do. The Croats refused to let them move into their houses. To which Vehbija Karic allegedly responded, 'Kill them, throw them into the lake,' that his men had understood this literally and that as a result, the crime had been committed." Did you tell that to the assembled people in Zuka's flat on that occasion??

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that Vehbija Karic said that but on this particular occasion, I wasn't there, and I don't recall him saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There is just a piece of transcript I want to put to you. Just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours at, 18th of March, page 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm sorry for interrupting you. Your Honour, I've just had our case manager who speaks the language look at the -- the real document and from that what I'm [inaudible] says -- this document says he wasn't sure whether it was Malco or the witness who is saying these things in the last part of our -- the context of the document, and that's what the -- the original Bosnian, there is a notation in writing as to who is supposed to have said that. So perhaps counsel would like to make it clear, that it wasn't in fact clear whether it was Mr. Delalic or Mr. Malco who actually made these utterances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you want, Mr. Morrissey, there is a request from Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think it's -- yes, Your Honour, in that light I'll clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, just to -- so that we can clear that up quickly. As far as you're concerned you didn't say any of those things and Malco didn't say those things in your presence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about this document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So Mr. Delalic, can I put this to you now? The truth of the matter is that you did cover up the crimes at Grabovica because you knew your soldiers were involved. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, I still stand by the fact that this crime was not committed only by soldiers of the 9th Motorised Brigade. I believe that soldiers from other brigades also committed the crime. Even these refugees who were on the other bank. At the time, also, I didn't have any idea exactly who these people were and future investigations will determine exactly who was involved. However, what you are saying is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour that's the end of that passage. I think we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, 20 May 2005 at 9.00 a.m.
